Profile and Plans forms: spacing and desktop-width fixes

UI audit · Proposal

Profile and Plans forms: spacing and desktop-width fixes

Every form and panel that shares the Paycycle padding bug or the oversized Add plan layout, each with circled screenshots and a tested CSS/markup fix.

  • Updated2026-11-07
  • Scopemy_finance · @ 3f533eb
  • Screens5 affected · 7 checked fine
  • Viewport1680 px desktop, dark

The answer: four shared CSS gaps break five screens

Short answer

The Paycycle bug and the oversized Add plan form are not one-offs. They come from four rules shared by every panel in UserProfile.css. The same gaps affect three more screens: Add income, Create MCP token and the Plans summary. About 40 lines of CSS and three small markup edits fix all five. Each fix was rendered with the app's real stylesheets (before/after images below).

5screens affected (2 reported + 3 found)
4shared root causes
8small CSS fixes (F1–F8), 3 markup edits
  1. A global label rule leaks into option rows. .user-profile label sets flex-direction: column. .profile-pref never resets it, so every option row whose root is a <label> is stacked and centered. S1S2 VERIFIED
  2. Page-level header and action bar are reused inside a card. .profile-panel-head and .profile-actions have no padding, so inside a card they touch the border. S4 VERIFIED
  3. Nothing caps the width on desktop. .user-profile, .profile-shell and .profile-panel have no max-width. Forms and lists stretch to the full window: 1390–1630 px at a 1680 px window. S9 VERIFIED
  4. Fixed grids don't match the number of items. The 2-column form grid leaves half-empty rows. The 3-column summary strip gets 5 items on the Plans page. The 2-column explainer gets 3 items. S6S11 VERIFIED

How the screens were checked

Each screen was rebuilt as a static page. The page loads the app's real globals.css, UserProfile.css and Plans.css, uses markup copied from the component, and fills in sample data. Each page was screenshotted in dark mode with headless Chromium at a 1680 px wide window. The same page was then shot again with the proposed fix.css added. S14

The two reproductions match your screenshots pixel for pixel in layout: the centered radios, the merged "Calendar monthA period…" text, the flush Save button and the 50/50 grid with an empty right half. That confirms the CSS alone causes them, not data or runtime state. S13

Limits. The three newly found screens were not checked in the live app, because that needs a signed-in session. Their markup is copied from the source files listed in each section. The app's top navigation is not drawn. Its real width is smaller than 1680 px, but the stretching scales with any desktop width. INFERRED (live screens not opened)

Which root cause hits which screen

Fix the four causes once in the shared stylesheet, and all five screens improve together. The matrix shows where each one appears.

Root cause × screen. Rule locations are in src/styles/UserProfile.css unless noted.

Paycycle — "How are you paid?" (reported)

Point: the card has no inner gutter at the top and bottom, and every option row is a centered column. Two CSS rules fix both, with no markup changes. src/components/BudgetPeriodSection.tsx

  1. Header flush to the border. The card reuses the page-level .profile-panel-head, which has no padding (R2). The icon also sits above the title's baseline because h3 has no flex styling. S3S4
  2. Centered column, text run together. The row is a <label class="profile-pref">, so it inherits flex-direction: column (R1). .profile-pref > div:first-child stacks title over hint, but here the wrapper is a <span>, so the rule never applies and "Calendar month" runs into its hint. S1S2S3
  3. "Show by" looks out of place. It is a <div> row, so it stays left-aligned while its options are centered.
  4. Save / Cancel flush to the border. EditorActions renders .profile-actions, which has no padding (R2). S5

Proposed fix

Keep the markup. A <div> inside a <label> is invalid HTML, so the fix targets the <span> wrapper in CSS rather than renaming it. Scope the padding to headers and action bars that sit directly inside a card form, so the Sign-out card and the avatar form are unchanged.

/* F1 — option rows: text left, radio right; title over hint */
.user-profile label.profile-pref { flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: nowrap; cursor: pointer; }
.user-profile label.profile-pref:hover { background: var(--bg-card-hover); }
.user-profile label.profile-pref > span:first-child { min-width: 0; max-width: 60ch;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.user-profile label.profile-pref input[type='radio'] { flex: none; width: 18px; height: 18px; accent-color: var(--primary); }

/* F2 — header / action bar inside a card get the 20px card gutter */
.user-profile .profile-card > .profile-panel-head { padding: 16px 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-color); }
.user-profile .profile-card > .profile-panel-head h3 { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; }
.user-profile .budget-period-hint > span { flex: 1 1 24ch; min-width: 0; }
.user-profile form.profile-card > .profile-actions { justify-content: flex-end; padding: 14px 20px;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border-color); background: var(--profile-sunken);
  border-radius: 0 0 var(--radius-lg) var(--radius-lg); }
Found while testing F3: with a narrower card, the first hint (.budget-period-hint, Plans.css:40) pushed its icon onto its own line. The hint is a wrapping flex row and its text <span> has no flex or min-width. The .budget-period-hint > span line in F2 fixes this. S12

Add plan form (reported)

Point: the form fills the window, and its two-column grid leaves half-empty rows. Capping the width and merging the time and date rows fixes it. src/components/PlannedSpendings.tsx

  1. Empty right half next to "What". The form body is a 2-column grid. Only its first child (Quick start), fieldsets and .income-dates rows span both columns. "What" is a plain label, so it takes one column. S6S7
  2. "At" alone on its row. "At" shares an .income-dates row with "Every", which only renders for some frequencies. For Once, Daily and Weekdays, half the row is empty. S7
  3. Selected option hard to see. The checked segment is --bg-card on --profile-sunken, two dark greys. Each of the 5 segments is about 315 px wide. S8
  4. Form and list span the whole window (R3). There are about 1200 px between a plan's name and its amount, so the eye has to cross the whole screen. S9

Proposed fix

/* F3 — readable width on desktop */
.user-profile > .profile-identity,
.user-profile > .profile-shell { width: 100%; max-width: 1180px; margin-inline: auto; }
.user-profile > .profile-panel { width: 100%; max-width: 960px; margin-inline: auto; }

/* F4 — no half-empty rows */
.user-profile .income-form-body > .income-field-full { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
.user-profile .income-dates { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr)); }

/* F5 — the chosen segment is unmistakable */
.user-profile .income-segment input:checked + span { background: var(--profile-soft); color: var(--primary);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--primary); font-weight: 600; }

Markup in PlannedSpendings.tsx: add income-field-full to the "What" label (line 246). Merge the two .income-dates blocks (lines 305–336) into one, so Every, At, Starts and Ends flow together. With auto-fit, a row has 2–4 fields and no holes.

<label className="income-form-group income-field-full"> … What … </label>

<div className="income-dates">
  {UNIT[draft.frequency] && (<label …>Every …</label>)}
  <label …>Starts / On …</label>
  {draft.frequency !== 'once' && (<label …>Ends …</label>)}
  <label …>At …</label>
</div>

Add income form (found)

Point: this is the same .income-form as Add plan, so it has the same width and selected-state problems. It also has one markup quirk: a checkbox inside an uppercase field label. Profile → Income, src/components/IncomeSources.tsx

  1. 1392 px wide form (R3). Six frequency segments of about 220 px each. S9
  2. "Monthly" is selected, but you can barely tell. Same rule as Add plan. S8
  3. Checkbox styled as a field label. The sentence "Paid on Friday when the payday is a weekend" is inside .income-form-label, so it renders in small uppercase grey. The native checkbox sits on the text baseline. S10

Proposed fix

F3 and F5 come for free. Add F6, and change lines 278–282 of IncomeSources.tsx to a plain checkbox label:

/* F6 — a checkbox is a sentence, not an uppercase field label */
.user-profile label.income-check { flex-direction: row; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
  font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 400; color: var(--text-main); }
.user-profile label.income-check input { width: 16px; height: 16px; accent-color: var(--primary); }

<label className="income-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked={…} onChange={…} /> Paid on Friday when the payday is a weekend
</label>

Create MCP token form (found)

Point: this form works around R2 with an inline style={{ padding: '20px' }}. Its three fields stack at full width (1350 px selects for short choices), and the action bar is left-aligned unlike every other form. Profile → AI & MCP, src/components/McpAccessSection.tsx

  1. Form is 1392 px wide, and the two short selects take a full row each. S15
  2. Save / Cancel are left-aligned and sit inside the padding, with no footer line. Add plan and Add income put them right-aligned in a footer. S5S15
  3. Token rows stretch the same way (R3). The new-secret card below also uses three inline styles (lines 234, 240, 254).

Proposed fix

Drop the inline padding and add class mcp-form. The fieldset gets the gutter and a 2-column grid, and the action bar reuses F2's footer. The inline styles of the secret card should become classes in the same edit. INFERRED (secret card not rendered).

/* F8 */
.user-profile .mcp-form { gap: 0; }
.user-profile .mcp-form > fieldset { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 16px 20px; padding: 20px; }
.user-profile .mcp-form > fieldset > label:first-child { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
@media (max-width: 760px) { .user-profile .mcp-form > fieldset { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }

<form className="profile-card profile-form mcp-form" noValidate …>   {/* no style prop */}

Plans page summary strip and explainer (found)

Point: the Plans page puts 5 totals into a 3-column strip and 3 notes into a 2-column grid. Both wrap and leave a hole. src/components/PlansPage.tsx

  1. 5 totals in 3 columns. .profile-summary is fixed at repeat(3, …), which was written for the 3-item strips on Income and Plans. "Estimates" and "Left this period" wrap to a second row with no divider above it and an empty third cell. "Left this period" is the most important number, yet it lands in that half-empty second row. S11
  2. 3 notes in 2 columns. .plans-explain is 1fr 1fr, so the third note ("Pay and income sources…") sits alone on a second row. S11

Proposed fix

/* F7 — strips fit their item count */
.user-profile .profile-summary { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr)); }
.user-profile .plans-explain   { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
@media (max-width: 760px) { .user-profile .plans-explain { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }

The existing phone rule (:256) still collapses the strip to one column, so mobile is unchanged. S11

Rolling it out

  1. CSS: append F1–F8 to src/styles/UserProfile.css (F7's .plans-explain line goes in Plans.css). All selectors are scoped under .user-profile, like the existing rules.
  2. Markup (3 edits): PlannedSpendings.tsx (the What class and merged date row), IncomeSources.tsx (the checkbox label), McpAccessSection.tsx (inline padding → mcp-form).
  3. Check at three widths: 1680 px (desktop), 900 px (narrow window, rail plus panel) and 390 px (phone). The phone layout uses its own rules at max-width: 768px. F3 only sets a maximum, so it cannot widen anything on a phone. INFERRED (phone width not shot)
  4. Regression watch: F1 changes every label.profile-pref. Today only two elements match, both option lists in BudgetPeriodSection.tsx (lines 152 and 188). The other .profile-pref rows are divs and are untouched. S3

Open questions

  • Width caps. 960 px for a single panel and 1180 px for rail plus panel were chosen to keep forms around 900 px. Do you want the panel centered (as proposed) or left-aligned under the app's navigation? OPEN
  • Selected-state colour (F5). The proposal uses the soft primary tint with a primary outline. A solid primary fill is the stronger alternative. OPEN
  • Not covered here: mixed date formats (the list shows Ended 2026-11-05, the form uses dd/mm/yyyy) and mixed money formats (15k chips vs 15.000 ₫). These are content consistency issues, not spacing. OPEN
